data.description:
## Observation

`binding_jira_key_map` (src/rebar/_ids.py) calls `_load_binding_reverse`, which `json.load`s the whole `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json` to read only its `reverse` index. On a copy of the live store, 2026-10-29, the file is 22.1 MB and the call peaks at 66.4 MB of traced memory to return a 5,623-entry map. `search_state` calls it once per search. After humdrum-priestly-lcont removed the reduce-loop retention, this load is the whole remaining search peak (66.4 MB of 66.4 MB). `audit_binding_drift` loads the same file for its own use, so its 66.4 MB is the same cost. Not yet checked: which other readers (`_resolve_via_binding_store` during id resolution) pay it per call, and what share of the file is `reverse`.

## Plan
1. Measure the size of each top-level key of bindings.json on a store copy, and count the per-call loads on the search and resolve paths.
2. Pick the remedy from the measurement: a per-process cache keyed on the file's (mtime_ns, size), or a streamed read of only the `reverse` key. Record the choice and why on this ticket.
3. Test that the map is unchanged and that a rewritten bindings.json is picked up on the next call.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `binding_jira_key_map` returns the same map as today on a copy of the live store.
- [ ] Its peak traced memory on that copy, before and after, is recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] A test shows a changed bindings.json is read on the next call.

## File impact (expected)
- src/rebar/_ids.py
data.title: search parses all of bindings.json to read its reverse index
